name: Question 3
problem: Which of the following sets of parametric equations, defined for $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ),$ generate the horizontal parabola given by the Cartesian equation $(y-5)^{2}=2(x-2)?$
worked_solution:
The parametric equations of a horizontal parabola $(y-k)^{2}=4p(x-h)$ that has its vertex at $(h,k)$ are

$$
x-h=p{t}^{2},\,y-k=2pt,
$$

where $p$ is constant.

Comparing the given Cartesian equation with the general case $(y-k)^{2}=4p(x-h),$ we see that the parabola has its vertex at $(h,k)=(2,5).$ So we have

$$
x-2=p{t}^{2},\,y-5=2pt.
$$

Now, comparing the right-hand sides of the given Cartesian equation and the general case, then solving for $p,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}4p(x-h) & =2(x-2) \\ 4p(x-2) & =2(x-2) \\ 4p & =2 \\ p & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the parametric equations of the parabola are

$$
x-2=(\frac{1}{2}){t}^{2},\,y-5=2(\frac{1}{2})t,
$$

which simplify to

$$
x-2=\frac{1}{2}{t}^{2},\,y-5=t.
$$

Question 3
?

Which of the following sets of parametric equations, defined for t∈(−∞,∞), generate the horizontal parabola given by the Cartesian equation (y−5)2=2(x−2)?

a
x−5=t,y−2=12t2
b
x−2=12t2,y−5=2t
c
x−2=12t2,y−5=t
d
x−5=12t2,y−2=t
e
x+2=12t2,y+5=t
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

The parametric equations of a horizontal parabola (y−k)2=4p(x−h) that has its vertex at (h,k) are

x−h=pt2,y−k=2pt,

where p is constant.

Comparing the given Cartesian equation with the general case (y−k)2=4p(x−h), we see that the parabola has its vertex at (h,k)=(2,5). So we have

x−2=pt2,y−5=2pt.

Now, comparing the right-hand sides of the given Cartesian equation and the general case, then solving for p, we get

4p(x−h)=2(x−2)4p(x−2)=2(x−2)4p=2p=12.

Therefore, the parametric equations of the parabola are

x−2=(12)t2,y−5=2(12)t,

which simplify to

x−2=12t2,y−5=t.
